source: Yale IIIF canvas 1006198, f69r; complete image 2793x3763 and two bounded details inspected natively
prior_exposure: The project had already inspected public f69r scans and color geometry; this new inspection is postexposure, one physical page, not independent confirmation.

radial_text_loci_from_prior_GDT1068.individual_locus_to_pixel_map: not independently established without transcribing/choosing a reading
radial_text_loci_from_prior_GDT1068.observation: Text is written in many radial compartments between fine brown division lines; it has no visible discrete arrow/leader from any one written item to a uniquely named bearing. The panel does not supply a twenty-two-to-twelve owner mapping.

colored_spokes.observation: Broad green and blue painted bars terminate at small perimeter lobes; four axes are unpainted in the old sixteen-position class inventory. Unequal brush ends do not form reliable pointing arrows.

orientation_candidates.central_motif: Eight-armed ochre star-like form, unevenly drawn but with no identified north/east/west/south or one-way direction marker.
orientation_candidates.other_marks: The page number 69 at the upper right and the side marginalia are not integrated compass bearings.

uncertainty: Very pale ink and decorative extensions could conceal a trace, but none is unambiguously an authorial label-to-bearing leader. This is a visual capacity judgment, not a palaeographic decipherment.
